macro.event: International Trade in Goods and Services, July
macro.note: Prior -$73.3bn for June; goods deficit $102.1bn, services surplus $28.8bn, May revised to -$77.6bn. Date and time confirmed on the BEA's own release schedule. The July advance goods deficit was already published at $118.8bn, up $17.4bn and the widest since March 2025, which skews risk toward a materially wider headline. BEA revises the prior month in every release.

Time confirmed on the BLS release schedule. The correct comparison for a revision release is the Q2 preliminary estimate of +1.4% productivity and +1.3% unit labour costs, not the Q1 figure of 0.8% that at least one aggregator listed as prior.

macro.event: Fed Governor Waller - speech, Economic Outlook
macro.note: Reuters NEXT Newsmaker interview, virtual. Listed on the Federal Reserve Board's own September calendar as a speech with a topic, not an informal appearance. POLICY-RELEVANT: he is the last Fed voice before the September 15-16 FOMC blackout begins Saturday September 5, and he speaks the day before August payrolls.

macro.event: S&P Global US Services PMI, August final
macro.note: August flash was 56.8 against 54.6 in July, with the flash composite at 56.0 against 54.5. A 56.8 S&P services reading against an ISM consensus near 54.2 is an unusually wide divergence between the two surveys and should be flagged rather than reconciled.

Prior 54.1, verified on ISM's own July report page, which was up from 54.0 in June and a 25th consecutive month of expansion. Consensus is 54.2 to 54.3 - the 54.5 figure in circulation was the JULY consensus, which missed, and must not be recycled. Employment sub-index prior 47.4 is contractionary and is the line to read ahead of tomorrow's payrolls; business activity prior 59.1.

macro.event: Employment Situation, August - THE WEEK'S EVENT
macro.note: Prior -23,000. Brief this as a SPREAD, not a point estimate, because the range of named professional forecasts is extraordinary: Fifth Third -25K, Barclays +25K, BofA +40K, Newsquawk +45K, Bloomberg consensus roughly +55K, Reuters poll +58K with 4.1% unemployment, Nomura +60K, Wolfe and Goldman and Credit Agricole +65K, Wells Fargo +80K, Capital Economics +90K. Note that a Goldman +60K/4.3% figure in circulation is a September 2025 artifact - the 2026 Goldman number is +65K with 4.1%. Unemployment consensus clusters 4.1% to 4.2%; average hourly earnings consensus +0.2% with Wolfe at +0.35%.
US equity and bond markets closed for Labor Day.

macro.event: Bank of Canada decision; ECB Governing Council convenes Berlin
macro.note: The ECB meets in Berlin September 9 and 10 with markets pricing a rate increase at more than 95% probability. Canada's counter-tariff measures are also scheduled for September 8.
First of the two inflation prints before the FOMC.
The last major inflation reading before the September 15-16 FOMC, and the single most important scheduled release of the month. University of Michigan sentiment also lands September 11.

Market prices 38.8% hold and 61.2% for a 25 basis point hike as of the September 2 FedWatch cohort. Probability of a cut is zero. Retail sales land September 16, the Bank of England September 17, and the Bank of Japan September 17-18.
